clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Ischemic Stroke evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Ischemic Stroke is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Management requires immediate stroke-team activation, glucose assessment, and noncontrast head CT to exclude hemorrhage; IV thrombolysis is used only when the patient meets eligibility criteria, with vascular imaging to assess for thrombectomy when indicated.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden right arm weakness and slurred speech 1h ago

Key HPI features: A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with sudden right arm weakness and slurred speech 1h ago. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Hypoglycemia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Exact time of onset critical.
management_principles: Activate the stroke team, check fingerstick glucose, obtain noncontrast head CT, assess IV thrombolysis eligibility, and obtain vascular imaging for possible thrombectomy when indicated
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
